evals.prompt: Write the entry point for a new Neovim plugin called trailblazer.nvim. Output one code block containing only lua/trailblazer/init.lua with: a setup() that merges user options over defaults, and a :Trail user command registered through the API that prints a placeholder message. Keep it under about 60 lines and do not implement the MRU storage, save/load, or tests.
evals.expected_behavior: Produces a compact, complete entry-point file: setup() with merged defaults and API-based command registration.
assertions: Shows the contents of lua/trailblazer/init.lua in a single code block
Defines a setup() function that merges user options over defaults
Registers the :Trail command with vim.api.nvim_create_user_command
Keeps the file compact rather than implementing storage, save/load, or tests

evals.prompt: Set up CI with selene, stylua, and plenary for this Neovim plugin repo. It's called waystone.nvim.
evals.expected_behavior: Creates .github/workflows/lint.yml and test.yml with selene, stylua, and plenary on stable + nightly.
assertions: Creates lint workflow with selene and stylua
Creates test workflow with plenary on stable and nightly Neovim
Checks out plenary.nvim as a sibling directory
Uses rhysd/action-setup-vim for Neovim installation

evals.prompt: Fix the LSP configuration in my init.lua — mason-lspconfig isn't setting up gopls correctly.
evals.expected_behavior: Treats this as user-config work and follows the config path (real config root, plugin manager, matching validation) rather than plugin development.
assertions: Does not scaffold plugin structure
Follows the config path for user configuration editing

evals.prompt: Add a :Glimpse command and a <leader>gp keymap to my existing plugin, glance.nvim. Make sure both are testable.
evals.expected_behavior: Registers the command with vim.api.nvim_create_user_command and the keymap with vim.keymap.set rather than vim.cmd strings.
assertions: Registers the command with vim.api.nvim_create_user_command
Registers the keymap with vim.keymap.set
Does not define the command or keymap with vim.cmd string syntax
Places the registration in the plugin module or plugin/ entry point

evals.prompt: Users who call require('glance').setup() twice end up with duplicate autocommands and keymaps. Fix setup() so repeated calls are safe.
evals.expected_behavior: Makes setup() idempotent so repeated calls do not duplicate registrations.
assertions: Makes setup() idempotent and safe to call multiple times
Guards against duplicate autocommand or keymap registration
Does not rely on telling users to call setup only once

evals.prompt: When a user passes setup({ window = { border = 'rounded' } }) the nested defaults under window disappear. Keep the defaults while honouring the override.
evals.expected_behavior: Merges user options over defaults with a deep merge while keeping defaults on the module config table.
assertions: Uses vim.tbl_deep_extend('force', ...) or an equivalent deep merge
Keeps defaults on the module config table such as M.config
Does not replace the defaults table wholesale with the user options
Preserves unspecified nested defaults

evals.prompt: Our plenary tests pass locally but fail in CI, apparently because the test bootstrap loads the developer's full Neovim config.
evals.expected_behavior: Uses a minimal_init.lua that does not load the user config and runs tests through the repo's make target.
assertions: Uses a minimal_init.lua that does not load the user's full config
Runs the specs through the repo's make test or equivalent target
Places specs under tests/ using the plenary structure

evals.prompt: Set up GitHub Actions for my plugin waystone.nvim so lint and tests both run, including against a development Neovim build.
evals.expected_behavior: Creates lint and test workflows that run selene plus stylua and plenary tests on stable and nightly Neovim.
assertions: Run lint with selene and stylua
Run plenary tests on both stable and nightly Neovim
Checks out plenary.nvim as a sibling directory
Installs Neovim through a setup action or equivalent pinned install

evals.prompt: Our plugin ships without documentation, so :help glance fails. Add proper help documentation.
evals.expected_behavior: Maintains a vimdoc file under doc/ with help tags so :help works after install.
assertions: Creates or updates doc/<plugin>.txt vimdoc
Includes help tags and a header compatible with :help
States that :help <plugin> should render after the change
Avoids putting the only documentation in README markdown

evals.prompt: Set up release automation for my plugin and make sure it still installs cleanly for lazy.nvim users.
evals.expected_behavior: Tags v* releases and keeps lua/ and doc/ at the repo root for lazy.nvim compatibility.
assertions: Tags releases as v* through GitHub Actions or an equivalent workflow
Keeps lua/ and doc/ at the repository root
Does not move runtime files into a nested packaging directory
Connects the release path to lazy.nvim installation compatibility

evals.prompt: My plugin's init.lua has grown to 600 lines covering commands, highlighting, and state. Restructure it.
evals.expected_behavior: Splits features into their own lua/<plugin>/<feature>.lua modules while keeping init.lua as the entry point.
assertions: Splits features into separate lua/<plugin>/<feature>.lua modules
Keeps init.lua as the module entry point
Keeps setup() and config defaults reachable from the entry point
Does not leave all logic in the single init.lua file

evals.prompt: A contributor suggests defining our commands with vim.cmd('command! Glimpse lua require("glance").glimpse()') because it is shorter than the API call. Should we take it?
evals.expected_behavior: Rejects vim.cmd string definitions in favour of the Neovim API for commands and keymaps.
assertions: Rejects the vim.cmd string approach for command definition
Recommends vim.api.nvim_create_user_command instead
Gives a concrete reason such as escaping, testability, or error visibility
Does not accept the suggestion on brevity grounds

evals.prompt: Our plugin tests assert that internal helper functions were called with specific arguments. A refactor broke them all even though behaviour is unchanged. Fix the test approach.
evals.expected_behavior: Rewrites tests to assert observable behaviour rather than internal implementation details.
assertions: Rewrites tests to assert observable behaviour
Avoids asserting that internal helpers were called with specific arguments
Keeps the specs in the plenary structure under tests/
Explains that implementation-coupled tests make refactors look like regressions

evals.prompt: A user calls setup({ highlight = false }) and every other default stops working. Trace what is wrong and fix it.
evals.expected_behavior: Deep-merges the partial options over defaults so the other defaults survive, including explicit false values.
assertions: Deep-merges the partial options over the defaults
Keeps the other defaults working after a partial setup call
Preserves an explicit false value rather than treating it as unset
Keeps the resolved config on the module config table

evals.prompt: We maintain our documentation in README.md but want doc/glance.txt vimdoc too. How should we wire that up?
evals.expected_behavior: Uses a markdown-to-vimdoc tool or an explicit vimdoc source, kept in doc/ and runnable from the repo tooling.
assertions: Uses a markdown-to-vimdoc path such as panvimdoc or lemmy-help, or maintains vimdoc directly
Keeps the generated help at doc/<plugin>.txt
Wires generation into the Makefile or CI so the file stays current
Verifies :help <plugin> renders in Neovim

evals.prompt: My plugin is failing to load and I think lazy.nvim is picking up the wrong checkout or XDG path. Where do I start?
evals.expected_behavior: Treats the config-side load failure with the config path rather than as plugin development.
assertions: Follows the config path for the config-side load failure
Does not scaffold plugin structure or plugin tests as the fix
Identifies the checkout or XDG path selection as the likely cause

evals.prompt: Add a :Glimpse command to my plugin that accepts an optional buffer number, supports a bang to force-refresh, and completes open buffers when tab-completing the argument.
evals.expected_behavior: Registers the command through the API with nargs, bang, and a completion function rather than parsing arguments by hand.
assertions: Uses vim.api.nvim_create_user_command with nargs and bang enabled
Supplies a completion callback that lists open buffers
Reads the optional buffer argument from the command opts table
Avoids hand-parsing the command line string for the bang or argument

evals.prompt: Users ask for a way to confirm my plugin is wired up correctly. Add a :checkhealth provider to glance.nvim.
evals.expected_behavior: Adds a health module under lua/<plugin>/health.lua that reports config and dependency state through the health API.
assertions: Creates a health module at lua/<plugin>/health.lua
Uses the health report API such as vim.health.start and vim.health.ok or warn
Reports meaningful state such as resolved config and dependency availability
States that :checkhealth <plugin> should show the report

evals.prompt: I need to rename a public function in my plugin without breaking users on the old name. What is the right way to handle the rename?
evals.expected_behavior: Keeps the old entry point as a wrapper that emits a deprecation warning through the API, with a documented removal path.
assertions: Keeps the old function name working as a wrapper rather than removing it outright
Emits the warning with vim.deprecate rather than a bare print or error
States a removal version or timeframe for the old name
Documents the rename in the help file under doc/<plugin>.txt

evals.prompt: My plenary specs pass individually but fail when run together. The plugin module keeps state between specs. How should the tests be structured?
evals.expected_behavior: Resets plugin state between specs so test order does not determine the result.
assertions: Identifies shared module state as the cause of order-dependent failures
Resets state between specs, for example in before_each
Avoids relying on spec execution order to isolate state
Keeps the specs behaviour-focused rather than asserting internal call details

evals.prompt: Add a `highlight` option to my existing Neovim plugin and a test for it.
evals.expected_behavior: Before editing, the agent identifies the plugin's actual entry point (lua/<plugin>/init.lua vs lua/<plugin>.lua) and checks whether tests and CI already exist, per the documented First move, rather than assuming a layout or bootstrapping new infrastructure that's already there.
assertions: Identifies the existing entry point (lua/<plugin>/init.lua or lua/<plugin>.lua) before editing.
Checks whether tests/ and CI already exist before adding new infrastructure.
Merges the new `highlight` option into config defaults with `vim.tbl_deep_extend("force", ...)` rather than replacing the whole config table.

evals.prompt: Add a :Glimpse command and <leader>gp keymap with plenary tests to my existing glimpse.nvim plugin.
evals.expected_behavior: The agent adds the one command, keymap, and its test in the appropriate feature module without restructuring the existing plugin layout, rewriting unrelated modules, or touching CI/docs unless the new command changes the documented interface.
assertions: Adds the :Glimpse command, keymap, and plenary test scoped to this one feature.
Does not restructure or rewrite unrelated existing modules, CI workflows, or docs that weren't asked about.
Uses vim.keymap.set and vim.api.nvim_create_user_command rather than vim.cmd string registration.

evals.prompt: I have a Neovim config checkout at ~/code/nvim-config and I launch nvim from that directory, but it still loads my live ~/.config/nvim config instead of the checkout. Set up the repro so I am actually testing the checkout.
evals.expected_behavior: Explains that cwd does not select the config, redirects configuration to the checkout explicitly, and validates by launching nvim.
assertions: States that the working directory does not determine which Neovim config loads
Redirects configuration to the checkout with XDG_CONFIG_HOME or an equivalent explicit config path, rather than relying on cd
Selects an app namespace with NVIM_APPNAME or explains why a dedicated namespace avoids clobbering the live config
Includes a validation step that launches nvim and confirms the checkout's config loaded

evals.prompt: The dashboard on Neovim startup shows the wrong layout and the statusline colours are off. When I run nvim --headless nothing appears. How should I validate the fix?
evals.expected_behavior: Uses a real TTY for UI-sensitive startup states instead of trusting a headless run.
assertions: Recommends a real TTY for dashboard, colour, and first-screen behaviour
Explains that headless runs can miss UI-sensitive startup state
Does not treat the empty headless output as proof the config is correct

evals.prompt:
Migrate this lazy.nvim plugin spec to vim.pack:

```lua
{ 'saghen/blink.cmp', branch = 'v1', opts = {} }
```

Give me the vim.pack entry.
evals.expected_behavior: Uses a real upstream repo with a verifiable pinned ref instead of lazy.nvim shorthand, keeping the blink v1 pin.
assertions: Uses the real upstream repository rather than a lazy.nvim shorthand name
Pins blink.cmp to the v1 branch or an equivalent version range
Avoids copying lazy.nvim-only spec keys into the vim.pack entry
Mentions verifying the reviewed target ref rather than trusting pack output blindly

evals.prompt: My Copilot completions work on the first request and then stop until I restart Neovim. The integration caches the Copilot client reference at setup time.
evals.expected_behavior: Reacquires the currently attached Copilot client per request instead of caching it.
assertions: Recommends reacquiring the attached Copilot client on each request
States that caching the client reference causes the stale behaviour
Validates the fix on the real attach path rather than assuming it works

evals.prompt: Reloading blink.cmp sources from my LspAttach handler throws an assertion about unknown providers.
evals.expected_behavior: Checks blink.cmp.config.sources.providers before reloading, since blink.reload asserts on unknown providers.
assertions: Checks blink.cmp.config.sources.providers before calling reload
Explains that blink.reload asserts on unknown providers
Avoids reloading providers that are not registered

evals.prompt: After vim.json.decode() some entries are vim.NIL and my list operations break with a type error.
evals.expected_behavior: Normalizes vim.NIL values after decoding before using the list.
assertions: Normalizes vim.NIL values after vim.json.decode
Performs the normalization before list operations
Does not treat vim.NIL as an ordinary table or list element

evals.prompt: On Neovim 0.12 my treesitter query handler errors when it calls :range() on a capture from iter_matches().
evals.expected_behavior: Unwraps the capture slot list before calling node methods on 0.12+.
assertions: Identifies that capture slots are lists on Neovim 0.12+
Unwraps the capture before calling node methods such as :range()
Keeps the query logic indexed against the actual capture semantics

evals.prompt: My statusline renders vim.ui.progress_status() with broken or doubled % markers.
evals.expected_behavior: Treats progress_status output as already statusline-formatted and stops double-escaping percent markers.
assertions: States that vim.ui.progress_status() already returns statusline-formatted text
Stops double-escaping the % markers
Validates the rendered statusline rather than only the string value

evals.prompt: I set a highlight extmark using positions from string.find() and the highlighted range clips the surrounding brackets.
evals.expected_behavior: Converts from 1-based inclusive string.find positions to 0-based end-exclusive extmark columns.
assertions: Explains that extmark columns are 0-based and end-exclusive
Explains that string.find positions are 1-based and inclusive
Adjusts the computed range so the brackets are not clipped
Checks the rendered highlight as the final verification

evals.prompt: A helper my LSP config relies on is nil during Neovim teardown, even though it works while editing.
evals.expected_behavior: Preloads the runtime helper on the LSP setup path instead of assuming LspAttach runs at teardown.
assertions: Recommends preloading the helper on the LSP setup path
States that LspAttach is not guaranteed to run during teardown
Verifies shutdown behaviour, not only in-editor behaviour

evals.prompt: Running stylua --check . and selene . fails in my Neovim config repo, apparently because of nested .worktrees checkouts.
evals.expected_behavior: Excludes nested .worktrees before trusting repo-wide validator output.
assertions: Excludes nested .worktrees/** from the repo-wide validators
Identifies the duplicate checkouts as the cause of the failures
Scopes validation to the intended config path before trusting the results

evals.prompt: I set a plugin option to false, but after my config merge it behaves as if the option were still true.
evals.expected_behavior: Preserves explicit false values with a ~= nil check rather than an and/or fallback.
assertions: Recommends checking ~= nil when merging option values
Warns against and/or ternaries that discard explicit false
Keeps the resolved value as false rather than falling back to a default

evals.prompt: I need a repeatable headless repro of a vim.pack startup problem that will not disturb my live Neovim installation.
evals.expected_behavior: Isolates all XDG directories together so synthetic plugins and lockfile state cannot leak into the live config.
assertions: Isolates XDG_CONFIG_HOME, XDG_DATA_HOME, XDG_STATE_HOME, and XDG_CACHE_HOME together
Explains that partial isolation can leak synthetic plugins or lockfile entries into the live config
Uses the isolated environment for the headless run

evals.prompt: After migrating to vim.pack the plugin is installed and its command exists, but the side effects from its config callback never happen.
evals.expected_behavior: Verifies the config callback side effect rather than treating package presence as proof of a working migration.
assertions: States that package presence or an exposed command does not prove the config callback ran
Recommends verifying the config callback side effect directly
Checks the pinned ref or review output as part of the diagnosis

evals.prompt: A failing Lua unit test in my file-sync service is throwing a nil index error. Help me find the root cause.
evals.expected_behavior: Routes generic debugging away from the Neovim config skill.
assertions: Routes to systematic debugging rather than the Neovim config workflow
Does not prescribe XDG, NVIM_APPNAME, or startup validation steps
Treats the failure as general Lua application code

evals.prompt: Write onboarding documentation that explains how our Neovim config is laid out and why certain plugins were chosen.
evals.expected_behavior: Routes documentation work away from the config-editing workflow.
assertions: Routes to the documentation co-authoring skill
Does not perform runtime validation or config edits as the primary work
Treats the task as explanation rather than behaviour change

evals.prompt: I ran a vim.pack update and it reported success, but the plugin is still on an older commit than the ref I pinned in my spec. Walk me through proving which ref is actually checked out.
evals.expected_behavior: Verifies the reviewed target ref against the pack output rather than trusting the success message.
assertions: States that a successful pack update does not by itself prove the pinned ref is checked out
Inspects the pack review output or the on-disk plugin state to confirm the resolved ref
Ties the check back to the ref declared in the plugin spec
Avoids suggesting a reinstall as the first step without diagnosis

evals.prompt: I set buffer-local options in after/ftplugin for one filetype, and when I open a second buffer of a different filetype the options stay applied. What is going on and how should the config be structured?
evals.expected_behavior: Explains buffer-local option leakage across filetypes and keeps the settings scoped to the intended ftplugin surface.
assertions: Identifies that buffer-local options set for one filetype can persist when switching buffers
Keeps the setting scoped to the ftplugin or after/ftplugin file for the intended filetype
Uses buffer-local option assignment rather than global option assignment
Suggests verifying by opening buffers of both filetypes

evals.prompt: gopls attaches to every buffer in my monorepo and resolves imports against the repository root, not the module I am editing. My LSP config uses a single root marker. How should the root resolution be fixed?
evals.expected_behavior: Adjusts LSP root resolution to the real project boundary instead of one repository-wide marker.
assertions: Identifies the single root marker as the cause of the wrong workspace root
Proposes root resolution based on the real module or project boundary
Keeps the fix inside the LSP setup path rather than adding a second plugin manager or overriding user state
Validates by checking the attached client's resolved root in the affected buffer

evals.prompt: My statusline throws errors on startup about a nil value from an LSP or diagnostic component, but only sometimes. How should I diagnose and fix it?
evals.expected_behavior: Traces the nil provider on the real startup path and validates in a real TTY, since the failure is UI-sensitive and intermittent.
assertions: Treats the intermittent failure as needing a real TTY startup check rather than only a headless run
Traces which statusline component returns nil before changing the rendering code
Guards the component against missing LSP or diagnostic state
Confirms the fix by starting Neovim and checking the rendered statusline

evals.prompt: Validate why this Neovim checkout still opens the live config instead of the worktree when I launch nvim.
evals.expected_behavior: Before trusting any repro or smoke test, the agent confirms the real config root and points `nvim` at the target checkout via `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` (set to the parent `.config` directory, not the repo root) and `NVIM_APPNAME`, rather than relying on `cd` alone.
assertions: Identifies the real config root and plugin manager before proposing a fix.
Sets `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` (to the parent `.config` dir) and `NVIM_APPNAME` to target the intended checkout rather than relying on `cd` alone.
Does not trust a repro result until it confirms which checkout `nvim` actually loaded.
deterministic_checks: sets XDG_CONFIG_HOME and NVIM_APPNAME before launching nvim to reproduce

evals.prompt: Add a new keymap and a treesitter textobject config to my Neovim setup, and make sure it doesn't break anything.
evals.expected_behavior: The agent keeps the smallest truthful implementation and validation scope: it implements the keymap/textobject change where the plugin lives, validates with the smallest mode that proves the behavior, and stops probing once the wiring is confirmed instead of re-running every repo-wide validator or restructuring unrelated config.
assertions: Scopes the change to the requested keymap/treesitter config without opportunistically restructuring unrelated plugin wiring.
Chooses the smallest validation mode that proves the change (targeted check) rather than an exhaustive re-validation of the whole config.
Excludes nested `.worktrees/**` when running repo-wide `stylua`/`selene` checks so duplicate checkouts don't produce false failures.
